title: Repository and local Maximum Polish state are split
implication: GitHub alone understates the local enrichment work; the ZIP alone cannot change repo status.
recommendation: Maintain this canonical state ledger and reconcile at every handoff.

title: Goals R02 is rejected after archive snapshot
implication: D-078 owner-review-candidate posture is superseded.
recommendation: Record D-079 and prohibit R02 inheritance as positive direction.

title: Maximum Polish lacks an early owner-fit gate
implication: Technical completeness can advance a visibly unacceptable concept.
recommendation: Install hard-fail owner-fit review before native implementation.

title: Goals R02 violates layered first-viewport product law
implication: The candidate erased Life Area/Goal/path continuity required by current canon.
recommendation: Use the R03 layered pursuit architecture.

title: Complete Today final package is missing from the ZIP
implication: Today approval can be trusted as ledger state but not independently re-reviewed or golden-master closed.
recommendation: Recover the referenced A1 R05 package before FR-2/golden-master closure.

title: Global Object Language R01 is blocked
implication: Its Passage/Row grammar is candidate evidence, not approved cross-root law.
recommendation: Rebuild shared grammar after Goals/You/global sessions provide approved evidence.

title: Maximum Polish accent usage conflicts with active canon
implication: SeaGlass/teal and canon violet-indigo cannot both be silently authoritative.
recommendation: Classify and resolve in FR-3; do not amend canon by implication.

title: Shell device viability remains unproven
implication: Simulator/UI proof cannot establish reach, edge gestures, optics, or real touch.
recommendation: Retain provisional status and execute physical-device matrix later.

title: Time R02 has the strongest bounded prototype evidence
implication: Time is a strong positive visual/interaction input but not production proof.
recommendation: Protect core direction and preserve explicit production/device ceiling.

title: Goals R02 proof is technically valid but selection-irrelevant
implication: Passing tests establish implementation behavior of a rejected concept.
recommendation: Keep proof as negative/process evidence; never cite it for selection.

title: Proof cost is front-loaded before concept validity
implication: Scarce Codex/build effort is spent on directions that a board review could kill.
recommendation: Adopt the seven-stage economic gate and stop-loss rules.

title: Goals needs a multi-layer adult first viewport
implication: Neither verbose R01 nor empty R02 satisfies the product.
recommendation: Approve/revise the written R03 architecture before one bounded candidate.

title: Truth and authority semantics are fragmented across families
implication: Proposed, accepted, external, stale, failed, recovered, and historical states risk inconsistent presentation.
recommendation: Adopt one epistemic grammar before trust/recovery enrichment.

title: State coverage is broad but incomplete and uneven
implication: Typical boards can hide missing empty/loading/error/interruption/restoration behavior.
recommendation: Use STATE_MATRIX.csv to drive only product-real gaps.

title: Accessibility evidence is mostly transformation intent, not manual proof
implication: Static AX frames cannot establish assistive-service behavior or focus restoration.
recommendation: Preserve transformation law and defer manual/device claims.

title: Localization and RTL evidence is selective
implication: Selected stress fixtures do not establish catalog, format, mixed-direction, or chronology resilience.
recommendation: Run high-risk matrix after concept selection.

title: Motion and haptics are specified more than proven
implication: Prototype recordings do not establish production continuity, haptic calibration, or performance.
recommendation: Use choreography as intent and require later device/runtime proof.

title: FR-2 entry conditions are not satisfied
implication: Goals, You, global sessions, trust/recovery, shared grammar, and corpus gaps remain unresolved.
recommendation: Keep FR-2 not begun; execute dependency-aware queue.

title: Design-to-production traceability is incomplete
implication: Approved provisional visuals may assume states/geometry not backed by current runtime.
recommendation: Complete FR-3 classification before any reconstruction contract.

title: Signature continuity can be diluted by generic UI polish
implication: Glass/cards/AI chat/calendar density are copyable and not the moat.
recommendation: Protect living day, temporal truth, pursuit continuity, owner routing, and humane recovery.

title: Golden-master coverage is incomplete
implication: Today package is missing and Goals has no selected direction.
recommendation: Limit current catalog to Shell/Time and recover/select missing families.

title: Prototype and juvenile appearance are owner hard fails
implication: A technically coherent design can fail immediately if it appears unfinished or childlike.
recommendation: Make maturity/perceived-intelligence automatic reject dimensions.

title: Positive grammar must exclude candidate and rejected evidence
implication: Mixing R01/R02/object-language candidates into the approved grammar corrupts authority.
recommendation: Derive invariants from approved families/current canon; use rejected work only negatively.

title: Cognitive infantilization is a systemic anti-pattern
implication: Agents may equate accessibility/low load with enlarged, simplified child UI.
recommendation: Use paired information-richness and maturity checks.

title: Cross-root density amplitude is unresolved
implication: The app risks feeling like unrelated expert and child products.
recommendation: Define one density ladder with root-specific amplitude.

title: Earlier calibration closure and Maximum Polish enrichment are different states
implication: Calling Search/Capture “closed” can obscure that their enrichment work is still queued.
recommendation: Use explicit terms: calibration closed; Maximum Polish enrichment not begun.

title: “Production-development-grade” language invites overclaim
implication: Readers may infer production/runtime readiness from prototype rigor.
recommendation: Use proof-class labels and exact ceilings in every packet.

title: Production implementation remains unauthorized
implication: Analytical/design outputs cannot be treated as a reconstruction contract.
recommendation: Keep FR-4 blocked until FR-2/FR-3 and owner authorization.

title: Future packets need immutable source snapshots
implication: Context drift and missing local evidence can recreate the orientation failure.
recommendation: Include source paths, hashes, decision IDs, and baseline commit in every packet.

title: Owner review must precede full adaptation proof
implication: The current sequence maximizes evidence for concepts not yet worth proving.
recommendation: Move representative board/native owner review before adaptation/full proof.

title: Reading burden and informational richness require paired gates
implication: Optimizing either word count or information density alone drives the product toward opposite failure poles.
recommendation: Score scan time, decision clarity, contextual richness, adult maturity, and deferred-detail recovery together before native proof.

title: FR-2 should receive compressed selected law rather than the entire corpus
implication: Passing the full ZIP or exhaustive vocabulary into FR-2 would reintroduce rejected, candidate, build-noise, and stale assumptions.
recommendation: Use the bounded handoff dossier, source hashes, protected decisions, unresolved questions, and proof ceilings as FR-2 input.
